sourceUseNotes.contribution: The January 2025 U.S. oral aripiprazole label lists schizophrenia, acute bipolar I manic or mixed episodes, adjunctive major-depressive-disorder treatment, autism-associated irritability, and Tourette disorder. Clozapine augmentation is not a listed indication; regulatory status is separate from comparative-effectiveness evidence.

A long-acting injectable aripiprazole formulation is listed in the United States for adult schizophrenia and bipolar I maintenance monotherapy. Formulation availability may inform adherence practicality, but it does not establish efficacy for long-acting aripiprazole used with clozapine.

In a Finnish nationwide observational cohort, clozapine plus aripiprazole was associated with lower psychiatric rehospitalization than clozapine monotherapy. This supports a real-world effectiveness signal, not causal proof, an acute symptom claim, or a general endorsement of antipsychotic polypharmacy.
